explanation: Compare the middle value with the right endpoint. If it is larger, the minimum lies to the right; otherwise the middle remains a possible minimum.
timeComplexity: O(log n) time for n distinct values.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: The minimum remains inside the current closed search interval. If nums[mid] exceeds the right endpoint, the rotation break and minimum lie strictly to the right of mid; otherwise mid may itself be the minimum and the interval can end there. Each update preserves the invariant until one candidate remains.
walkthrough: For [11,14,2,5,8], the middle value 2 is no greater than the right value 8, so keep the left portion including 2. Comparing 14 with that endpoint then discards the part before 2. Return the minimum value 2.
edgeCases: The array is nonempty and has distinct values.
An unrotated array has its minimum at index zero.
One value is already the answer.
